name: pslide_period
title: Slide along multiple inputs simultaneously relative to an index chunked by period.

origin.description: pslide_period() represents the combination of pslide() with slide_period(), allowing you to slide over multiple vectors at once, using indices defined by breaking up the .i-ndex by .period.

arguments.name: .l
arguments.text: A list of vectors. The length of .l determines the number of arguments that .f will be called with.

arguments.name: .i
arguments.text: The index vector, broken up by .period.

arguments.name: .period
arguments.text: The period to chunk .i by, passed to warp::warp_distance.

arguments.name: .f
arguments.text: A function applied to each window. A formula is accepted in R.

arguments.name: .before / .after
arguments.text: How far the window reaches in period-group space. Inf pins that edge.

arguments.name: .every / .origin / .complete
arguments.text: Forwarded to warp::warp_distance and the complete trimming logic.

origin.details: The output length equals the number of unique warp distance groups, optionally padded with missing values when .complete is TRUE.
origin.value: A list the length of the unique period groups.
origin.example: pslide_period(list(1:6, 7:12, i), i, "month", function(a, b, c) data.frame(x = a, y = b, i = c))

translation.description: Slide a function over parallel vectors using period groups from warp_distance on a datelike index.
translation.usage: pslide_period(items, i, period, f, *args, every=1, origin=None, before=0, after=0, complete=False)

arguments.name: items
arguments.text: A list of vectors. NumPy one-dimensional arrays are accepted.

arguments.name: i
arguments.text: A warp Date, POSIXct, or POSIXlt index.

arguments.name: period
arguments.text: The period string or value passed to warp.warp_distance.

arguments.name: f
arguments.text: Called with one window slice per list element, then any extra args.

arguments.name: before / after
arguments.text: How far the window reaches in period-group space. math.inf pins that edge.

translation.details: Calls warp.warp_distance, forms hop ranges on unique groups, and applies hop_index_apply like slide_period_common in R.
translation.value: A list. Missing positions are None.
translation.example:
from slider.pslide_period import pslide_period
from warp import Date
pslide_period([list(range(1, 7)), list(range(7, 13)), i], i, "month", lambda a, b, c: {"x": a, "y": b, "i": c})
